operations.label: MPE digestion
operations.description: Treat isolated nuclear chromatin with the MPE-Fe(II) complex. DNA strand breaks fragment the chromatin, preferentially through cleavage of linker DNA between nucleosomes. The digestion panel marks the chromatin with stars; the separated DNA-associated particles after the next arrow display the fragmentation outcome. The reagent is part of this local reaction, rather than a separate material branch.
operations.mechanism: The catalogue reports methidium-mediated intercalation of the MPE-Fe(II) complex into DNA and oxygen-dependent single- and double-strand breaks. The primary abstract reports preferential cleavage of linker DNA between nucleosomes with little sequence bias.
operations.information_effect: DNA accessibility and protection influence which fragments survive digestion. Their genomic DNA sequence and fragmentation boundaries carry an indirect record of chromatin organization for the downstream sequencing readout. The paper reports little sequence bias and preferential linker cleavage; neither establishes perfect sequence independence or perfect nucleosome specificity.

operations.label: DNA extraction
operations.description: Recover DNA from the digested chromatin, producing free DNA fragments represented by blue lines instead of DNA-associated gray particles. The extraction block is kept at the breadth shown.
operations.information_effect: Extraction yields DNA rather than protein-associated particles, retaining the recovered genomic fragments as the readout carrier. The abstract reports sequencing of MPE-digested nuclear material for chromatin structure analysis. Sequencing the recovered fragment population can support inference of chromatin organization; the reported histone-correlated and noncanonical-particle peaks mean that a recovered fragment does not itself identify a canonical nucleosome. The extracted DNA is the input interface to unshown library preparation, not an adapter-bearing library visibly produced here.

checks.rationale: The registered abstract indeed lacks this reagent, but leaving the resolved literature discrepancy only in a nonblocking Unknown does not supply the required evidence-backed correction. Independent inspection found that the original paper’s search-indexed Materials and Methods, Digestion with MPE-Fe(II), describes quenching; direct opening of that full-text page returned a browser challenge. The full correction paragraph at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6800311/ (PMID 31591251; DOI 10.1073/pnas.1916397116) corrects bathophenanthroline to bathophenanthrolinedisulfonate. These are external findings, not content of paper:26080409 in the registry. See supplementary_review_lookup.json for the independently inspected locators. Obtain registered versions of those two bounded passages, retain the drawn name, and add the specific quenching/identity interpretation in the designated correction fields for op_bathophenanthroline_addition and s_post_addition_chromatin. The unresolved evidence gap must prevent final scientific acceptance until represented; no further chemistry speculation is needed.
